title: 1-bit and 2-bit Characters
summary: We use two special characters: the first is encoded in one bit (0), and the second in two bits (10 or 11).
statement: We use two special characters: the first is encoded in one bit (0), and the second in two bits (10 or 11). Given an array of bits ending in 0, determine if the final bit represents the one-bit character.
constraints: bits is a valid encoding ending in zero.
A zero starts a one-bit character; a one starts a two-bit character. Determine whether the final zero stands alone.
reference_solution:
def final_character_is_one_bit(bits):
    index=0
    while index<len(bits)-1:index+=2 if bits[index] else 1
    return index==len(bits)-1
hints: Parsing is deterministic because each leading bit fixes the character width.
Walk from the start until reaching or passing the final index.
Advance one on zero and two on one while index<n-1; accept exactly when index==n-1.
There is no branching in a valid encoding, so the unique parse directly reveals whether the final zero begins its own character.
editorial: There is no branching in a valid encoding, so the unique parse directly reveals whether the final zero begins its own character.

tests.explanation: The first two bits form a two-bit character, leaving the final zero alone.
The encoding splits as 11 and 10, so the last zero belongs to a two-bit character.
